problem_meta.agent_answer:
**Most likely product: the de-Boc piperazine**, with the rest of the scaffold unchanged.

```smiles
COC1=CC=C2C(=C1C(C)N3CCNCC3)O/C(=C\C4=N[NH1]C5=CC=CC=C45)C2=O
```

The transformation removes the Boc group from one piperazine nitrogen, converting it to **N–H**. A close ORD match supports this deprotection and reports a 97% yield in 2 hours. The encoded components include 1,4-dioxane and chloroform; the matching record instead lists 1,4-dioxane and methylene chloride, so the match is close rather than exact. The isolated material could be an acid-addition salt; the structure above shows the neutral free base. (Evidence: `call_KDEsSAE6FDRmWnVhLG6ylkJg`, `call_kP9mz4hRLhbk2S9gHd4pgAoL`.)
